rationale: The assistant split the problem sensibly (dead vs powered-but-not-starting), correctly noted that a lit spur neon does not prove output, and gave a safe fuse-check with isolation at the consumer unit first ('Turn off the dishwasher circuit at the consumer unit first'). It stayed well calibrated, naming the fuse and internal power/control fault as 'two realistic causes' without asserting a diagnosis or a part, and escalated with the useful instruction to have the engineer 'test the spur output first before condemning dishwasher parts'. Weaknesses: it never asked make/model, and when the customer said they did not know how to check the fuse and had no spare, it escalated rather than briefly explaining the fuse drawer and that a correctly rated fuse is cheap to buy, which might have avoided a call-out.
